difficulty_reason: The lemma states both that the base change of a completely decomposed morphism of schemes is completely decomposed and that a completely decomposed family {X_i -> Y} remains so after any base change Y' -> Y. The retained proof is written: fix a point y' of Y' over y and a point x of X over y with kappa(x) = kappa(y); the fibre-product point dictionary (Schemes, lemma points-fibre-product) supplies a unique point x' of X' = X x_Y Y' over (y', x) with residue field kappa(x') = kappa(y'), obtained by the tensor product of fields computation kappa(x) tensor_{kappa(y)} kappa(y') = kappa(y') tensor kappa(y') whose unique prime is the diagonal; the stated uniqueness is exactly what turns the completely-decomposed condition at y into the one at y', and the family version is the identical argument applied to each member (the author's we omit the details covers only this mechanical reindexing). Retained author proof at lines 23175-23184.
